solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record originally cut by members of the Police

indicators.note: by means beside here, so the police officers sit next to the picked letter

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors, officers of the British police

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word cut

explanation.surface: A record is censored, at first, by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' reads like censorship, but 'by' only means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat circular plate, which is exactly what the shorter word names.

clue.text: University student receiving no money? On the contrary — plenty

parts.note: no is zero, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: receiving means one group of letters takes the other into its middle
on the contrary flips the surface so the money takes in the university student, not the other way round

parts.note: pence are British coins, so money in small change
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A penniless university student taking in cash, or rather the cash taking in the student, produces plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' swaps the roles in the surface: the money (O PENCE) does the receiving and U L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is wealth and abundance, a synonym for plenty in the sense of riches.

clue.text: Guitar's last note receding with echo effect

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word guitar
receding means going backwards, so the note's letters are read from the end

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A guitarist's final note fades away with an echoing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns BREVE into EVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverberation, shortened in studio jargon, is the echoing sound effect used on guitars and vocals.

clue.text: Flattering talk that keeps the filth at bay!

definitions.meaning: flattery used to persuade someone is called by this soapy name
a gentle liquid cleanser literally keeps dirt away

explanation.surface: Flattery that keeps the police away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the filth' is British slang for the police, which the surface wants; read literally it is dirt, removed by soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasive flattery is idiomatically named after a mild cleaning product, and that same product removes dirt.

clue.text: Having plenty, former US politician's golf comes first

indicators.note: comes first means the letter for golf is shifted to the front of the name

parts.note: Al Gore was US Vice President under Bill Clinton
golf is G in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A former US vice president, wealthy, puts his golf first.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of Gore moves to the front of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in abundance, so a place described this way is having plenty of something.

clue.text: After part of meal, ring kitchen porter

indicators.note: After places the ring following the course of the meal

parts.note: a dish is one course or item of a meal
a washer is a flat ring used with a bolt

explanation.surface: After eating part of a meal, someone phones the kitchen porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call but is a flat metal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen porter is the staff member who washes up dishes in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Small alcoholic drink in a colourful spot

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tipple is a person's favourite alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A small drink taken in a bright, colourful place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting with dots, so a single coloured dot is described by the term.

clue.text: Maniac MP rages about making this unnecessary!

definitions.text: Maniac MP rages about making this unnecessary!

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the three words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A raving MP rants so much that a deliberate campaign of slander would be superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an MP raging like a maniac does the damage to his own reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of slander damages a politician's reputation, needless when the politician behaves like a maniac.

clue.text: Duck alters places where eggs are housed

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, written O
varies means changes or alters

explanation.surface: A duck rearranges the places where she keeps her eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nought, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the female organs that produce and hold egg cells, a biological description.

clue.text: Insult spoken by ungracious fellow vanishing, showing skilful deception

indicators.note: spoken signals that the insult is heard, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub

indicators.note: vanishing says the fellow disappears from the curt word

parts.note: offhand means curt or ungracious

explanation.surface: A rude man utters an insult and then vanishes, a clever piece of trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vanishing' takes F out of OFFHAND, leaving OFHAND.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means a conjuring trick or any deft trickery, matching skilful deception.

clue.text: Wonderful girl in court going after former lover

indicators.note: going after puts the court-and-girl section behind the former lover

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wonderful girl in court pursuing her ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives of high praise, synonyms meaning outstandingly good.

clue.text: Paint church getting endlessly bored? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: getting here means taking something into it
quite the opposite reverses the surface so the trimmed word is what gets the church inside
endlessly takes off the first and last letters of the word bored

explanation.surface: A church being decorated gets tediously dull, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly bored' gives ORE; 'Quite the opposite' means ORE gets CH, not CH getting bored.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used as a paint colour.

clue.text: Fight navy in wreck

indicators.note: in puts the navy letter inside the word for wreck

parts.note: to ruin is to wreck

explanation.surface: A battle with the fleet in a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or skirmish, so a fight in informal speech.

clue.text: Mongrel turns tail having bitten a person who studies animals

indicators.note: having bitten means the jumbled letters close their jaws around the letter
mongrel means mixed, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mongrel spins round chasing its tail after biting a zoologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mongrel' says mixed breed in the surface but signals the jumble; 'having bitten' holds the A in its jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalist is a student of natural history, especially of animals and plants in the wild.

clue.text: Explosive sound resonated round capital of Estonia — it might come back!

indicators.note: round means the sound words surround the picked letter

parts.note: a boom is the noise of an explosion
rang means echoed or resonated

indicators.note: capital of points to the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A blast echoed around Tallinn, the Estonian capital, and might return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Estonia' tempts with Tallinn; it is only the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick that returns to the thrower is cryptically defined by its returning flight.

clue.text: Mashed potato father had without delay

indicators.note: mashed means crushed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad had mashed potato in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly or without hesitation, like a signal given by dropping a hat.

clue.text: Laugh at one copper left in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the three letter pieces inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a ride is a vehicle in informal use
one is I as a Roman numeral
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: People mock a lone policeman left behind in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule someone is to mock or make fun of them, the same as laughing at them.

clue.text: Arranging of stones and chains of flowers

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Setting out stones together with garlands of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Festoons are garlands or chains hung in loops, often of flowers.

clue.text: Bird to move away from high ground

parts.note: to part is to move away or depart
a ridge is a long stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: A bird has to leave the hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird of fields and hedgerows.

clue.text: Change destination

definitions.meaning: to ... is to order again, hence change
a holiday place people travel to

explanation.definitionFit: A holiday town is a destination; split as re-sort it means arrange differently, a change.

clue.text: Hostility seen in university in east New York

indicators.note: in puts the university's initials inside the letters for east and New York

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Animosity found at a university in the eastern part of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is the state of being enemies, a synonym for hostility.

clue.text: Burning passion's conveyed in return in part of letter

indicators.note: conveyed in return means the passion word is carried back the other way

parts.note: fire is burning passion, and the 's is read as a letter S

explanation.surface: A burning passion is expressed in a reply letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence but means a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing off a printed character in many typefaces.

clue.text: One day, Paul perhaps wastes time

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
Les Paul was a guitarist and the name of a famous electric guitar

explanation.surface: One day, a man named Paul, perhaps, is lazing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paul' looks like a first name, but LES is the first name of Les Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to do nothing useful, which is to waste time.

clue.text: This time I answer

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle calls himself Commoner, so I refers to that pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter says that this time they will reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter speaking, whose pseudonym is Commoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the dating system we live in now, so it is the present era.

clue.text: Freelancer's smuggling spirit

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something concealed inside, so the answer sits within the word

explanation.surface: A self-employed worker is smuggling alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests liquor but means verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair and verve are what this borrowed French word means, a lively spirit.

clue.text: Child gets away from big bird in the Netherlands — it smells!

indicators.note: in puts what remains of the bird inside the country code

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: gets away from means the child is removed from the bird

parts.note: the ostrich is the largest bird

explanation.surface: A child escapes from a large bird in Holland, and it stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets away from' removes the child letters from the bird; 'it smells' is the organ doing the smelling, not something smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is the opening of the nose, the organ through which one smells.

clue.text: Drank at 19 from a big cup

indicators.note: 19 refers to the answer of the clue at 19, meaning change, so the letters are changed around

explanation.surface: Someone drank at a holiday spot from a large cup.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' is RESORT, read here as re-sort, so DRANK AT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, often for beer, so a big cup.
